items.title: [@rog0x/mcp-docker-tools] @rog0x/mcp-docker-tools: executes arbitrary code via the handleImageList function
items.summary: An issue in @rog0x/mcp-docker-tools 1.0.1 allows a remote attacker to execute arbitrary code via the handleImageList function.Referenceshttps://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-106765https://github.com/rog0x/mcp-git-tools/issues/1https://stillosdigitalholdings.com/advisories/CVE-2026-106765.cve.jsonhttps://www.npmjs.com/package/@rog0x/mcp-docker-toolshttps://github.com/advisories/GHSA-fq6x-j3g6-xx83

items.title: [@nx/maven] @nx/maven and @nx/gradle have OS command injection via nx.json plugin options
items.summary: Summary@nx/maven and @nx/gradle spawn their project-graph analyzers through a shell and interpolate plugin options read from nx.json straight into the command line. Because a shell parses the whole line, an option value containing shell syntax is executed as a command by any nx command that constructs the project graph. Anyone who clones a hostile repository, or who checks out a pull request that edits nx.json, runs the injected command with their own privileges.SeverityA victim who runs an ordinary nx command in an attacker-supplied Maven or Gradle workspace gets code execution as themselves. In most such workspaces an attacker who can write nx.json can already run code through the repository's build files (./mvnw, pom.xml, and the Gradle equivalents), so the genuinely new exposure is narrow — for example CI building a fork's pull request where nx.json is writable but the build files are not. We have no evidence of exploitation in the wild.Affected & Patched VersionsPackageVulnerablePatched@nx/maven>= 22.0.2, < 22.7.9; >= 23.0.0, < 23.1.222.7.9, 23.1.2@nx/gradle>= 21.0.0, < 22.7.9; >= 23.0.0, < 23.1.222.7.9, 23.1.2[!IMPORTANT]Workspaces that register neither @nx/maven nor @nx/gradle in nx.json are unaffected — the vulnerable code only runs from those plugins' graph-construction paths, and no other Nx plugin shares this pattern.RemediationUpgrade to 22.7.9 (22.x line) or 23.1.2 (23.x line) or later:nx migrate 23.1.2Upgrade both nx and the affected plugin (@nx/maven and/or @nx/gradle). The plugin's fix depends on code that ships in the nx package, so bumping the plugin without a matching nx upgrade will not resolve it.There is no configuration to change — upgrading is the whole fix. If you cannot upgrade yet, only run nx commands in repositories you trust, since a malicious nx.json can execute code on a vulnerable version.DetailsBoth plugins spawn their analyzer through a shell and interpolate nx.json plugin options into the command, so those option values are shell source. For Maven the injectable value is the targetNamePrefix option; for Gradle it is broader, since every plugin option is mapped into a -P argument and arbitrary option names are accepted, making both the name and value of any option injectable.CreditsArkadiusz Marta (RE:SOURCE) — ReporterReferenceshttps://github.com/nrwl/nx/security/advisories/GHSA-qm8w-vx34-5j9jhttps://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-119282https://github.com/nrwl/nx/pull/36626https://github.com/nrwl/nx/commit/02c5d59e8dbbbe30963c0181c6a22cd8c1190a25https://github.com/nrwl/nx/commit/60196b7cfcffcada35b6b90e53bf1a78d049b548https://github.com/nrwl/nx/commit/c227f4780b054c512965c73aa480a48f9f781409https://github.com/nrwl/nx/releases/tag/22.7.9https://github.com/nrwl/nx/releases/tag/23.1.2https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-qm8w-vx34-5j9j
